q: How does the Medras-MC misrepair-vs-LET curve extend into FLASH and proton-minibeam regimes where dose-rate and spatial fractionation dominate?
basis: The paper's dose-rate machinery (Sec 2.3, Fig 6) was validated against Lehmann/Newman conventional dose rates. FLASH (>40 Gy/s) and minibeam geometries lie orders of magnitude outside the calibration window, yet the mechanistic MC backbone (fast/slow repair with rate constants ~2.1/h and ~0.26/h) should extrapolate cleanly if track structure is honestly resampled at those instantaneous dose rates.
next_steps: 1. Modify damageModel.basicXandIon to accept an instantaneousDoseRate override, seeding SDD generation at 1e2-1e3 Gy/s pulse profiles. 2. Compare Medras-MC predicted misrepair vs. published FLASH clonogenic data (Vozenin 2019 zebrafish/mouse survival). 3. Report divergence as a function of pulse duty cycle. No external paid data needed; FLASH survival tables are in supplementary of most FLASH papers.

q: Can modern DNA-repair pathway models (e.g., explicit MRE11-RAD50-NBN complex kinetics, 53BP1/RIF1 shieldin dynamics) be swapped into medrasrepair.py without breaking the two-exponential kinetics fit?
basis: The shipped code hard-codes a two-component repair model with rate constants lambda_f and lambda_s that lump NHEJ into 'fast' and HR-plus-NHEJ-on-complex into 'slow'. Recent single-molecule imaging (Britton 2020, Setiaputra 2019) resolves at least four kinetically-distinct pathways with cell-cycle-phase and chromatin-state dependence.
next_steps: 1. Fork medrasrepair.py and expose the rate-constant table as a JSON config. 2. Insert a 4-pathway model with published rate constants from Loffler 2018. 3. Re-run the 23-condition sweep and compare bi-exponential fit residuals. 4. Check whether high-LET carbon predictions shift enough to change the RBE-peak location.

q: How sensitive are Medras-MC predictions to the input LET spectrum (mono-energetic vs. Bragg-peak-realistic mixed spectra) for clinical proton therapy?
basis: This replication used mono-energetic proton tracks 1.77-29.78 keV/micrometer. Clinical spread-out-Bragg-peak (SOBP) beams sample a wide LET distribution at each depth, with an especially sharp LET rise in the distal fall-off region where RBE uncertainty matters most.
next_steps: 1. Generate synthetic SOBP LET spectra using TOPAS or the analytic Bortfeld model. 2. Run damageModel with per-voxel LET-weighted averages vs. properly-sampled spectra. 3. Quantify how much the misrepair-vs-depth curve differs between mono-energetic and spectrum-realistic inputs. Free code: TOPAS is open-source.

q: Which specific tumor cell lines (glioblastoma stem cells, chordoma, sarcoma) show the largest Medras-MC prediction error, and can that error map to a physical mechanism the model omits?
basis: The 2021 paper's Fig 4 MID scatter shows systematic outliers, but the paper does not diagnose them. Cell lines with abnormal repair phenotypes (BRCA1/2 loss, DNA-PKcs mutation, ATM-null) should map to specific Medras parameters (fast/slow branching ratio, complex-lesion misrepair probability).
next_steps: 1. Curate a small panel of cell-survival curves from cell lines with sequenced DDR-pathway variants (via cBioPortal or DepMap, both free). 2. Fit Medras parameters per line. 3. Report which parameters correlate with which mutation classes. 4. Test whether the residuals shrink when a mutation-class-specific parameter override is applied.

q: Can machine-learning parameter identification (Bayesian inference, neural posterior estimation) from clonogenic-survival assays make Medras-MC self-calibrating per cell line?
basis: Currently Medras uses a single global parameter set. Clonogenic assays measure survival at 5-10 doses per cell line; a modern amortized-inference network (e.g., BayesFlow, sbi) could invert those 5-10 measurements to a full Medras parameter posterior per line in seconds.
next_steps: 1. Build a simulator wrapper that emits survival curves from Medras parameter tuples. 2. Train a neural posterior estimator on 10k simulated parameter/curve pairs. 3. Validate on held-out published clonogenic assays. 4. Compare inferred parameters across radioresistant vs. radiosensitive lines. All-free stack: PyTorch + sbi + published clonogenic tables from open supplementary materials.
